topic: humanoid robot market: funding, manufacturers, deployments, IPOs, adoption

items.title: Unitree opens up 629% in its Shanghai debut
items.summary: The humanoid maker's shares opened at 1,100 yuan against an issue price of 150.80 in their STAR Market debut — a 629% pop — before closing their first day up 460% at 845 yuan, according to Reuters. The listing raised about $905 million, and Reuters counts Deep Robotics, Leju, Mech-Mind, X Square and AgiBot among the robot makers lining up to follow.

items.title: Robotera weighs a $1 billion Hong Kong IPO
items.summary: The Tsinghua-born maker of the L7 humanoid and XHand is reportedly considering a Hong Kong listing that could raise up to $1 billion, though no prospectus has been filed yet. Its robots already work in more than 10 logistics centers with China Post and SF Express, according to the company.

items.title: Unitree claims a 12.66 m/s sprint and a 2-meter jump
items.summary: An unnamed Unitree humanoid hit a top speed of 12.66 meters per second and cleared a 2 meter standing jump, figures the company frames as surpassing human records, according to a statement reported by Global Times. The robot was developed in just over three months, and the report does not specify the test surface, run distance or any independent verification of the numbers.

items.title: Robotis opens the books on its AI Sapiens K1
items.summary: South Korea's Robotis has put the K1 into production as a fully open source humanoid, with mechanical design, electrical resources, software, simulation assets and training workflows all meant to be shared, according to the company. The 135.5 cm, 35 kg research platform runs ROS 2 on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX and uses DYNAMIXEL quasi direct drive actuators.

items.title: Beijing's Humanoid Games add a home for 1,500 robots
items.summary: The second World Humanoid Robot Games open Saturday in Beijing with 666 teams and 2,056 robots from 16 countries and regions, a 138 percent jump in teams from the inaugural event, according to organizers. A new Robot Home facility can house more than 1,500 robots, charge at least 1,200 batteries and process check-in for a single robot in 30 seconds, CCTV Finance reported.

items.title: Robot makers are taking the side door to Wall Street
items.summary: The traditional IPO is no longer the presumptive route to public markets for robotics companies, two Mintz attorneys argue in The Robot Report — pointing to Agility Robotics' pending $2.5 billion SPAC merger with Churchill Capital and Serve Robotics' reverse merger as examples of the alternatives.

items.title: LG joins the humanoid race with NVIDIA inside
items.summary: LG signed a memorandum of understanding with NVIDIA and says it will unveil a bipedal humanoid built on Isaac GR00T, Jetson Thor and the Halos safety stack in the first quarter of 2027, drawing actuators, sensors and batteries from LG Electronics, LG Innotek and LG Energy Solution. The pact also covers an NVIDIA-powered AI factory in Cheonan slated to reach 80 MW by the first half of 2028, according to LG.

items.title: Roboto Origin opens up a $4,900 humanoid for makers
items.summary: Shanghai RoboParty's 125 cm, 34 kg prototype lists at $4,900 for research, education and hands-on development, with hardware, software, training workflows and assembly guidance shared for modification, according to the company. Its demos range from obstacle avoidance and sorting goods to threading a needle.

items.title: San Mateo County approves kill-switch rules for humanoids
items.summary: County supervisors unanimously passed a resolution requiring permits, emergency kill switches and fire-safety measures for commercial humanoid robots — one of the first US counties to adopt such a framework, according to the ABC7 report the story cites. Permit fees could help pay for specialized firefighting equipment, and the resolution gives the county a mechanism to track job displacement.

items.title: Swancor's $12,000 PrimeBOT Q1 enters production
items.summary: The 50 cm, 4 kg desktop humanoid from the Chinese composites group's robotics brand is aimed at fine work — sorting goods, assembling products and threading a needle, according to the company. Now in production after its CES 2026 debut, it is priced well below the cost of many larger humanoids.

items.title: Retail buyers bid $1.2 trillion for Unitree's IPO
items.summary: The retail tranche of Unitree's Shanghai listing was subscribed 5,526 times over, with individual investors placing 9.8 million orders worth about 8.1 trillion yuan ($1.2 trillion), according to an exchange filing cited by Bloomberg. That tops the retail book for memory chipmaker CXMT's offering last month — which Bloomberg called the second-biggest China debut ever — as Unitree heads for a roughly $9 billion valuation.

items.title: RoboStore launches Robo Inc. to build robots on US soil
items.summary: RoboStore — which says it has put more than 1,500 humanoid and quadruped robots into the field for some 4,500 North American customers — is moving upstream into manufacturing and systems integration with a new company, Robo Inc. According to the company, it will pair global robotics supply chains with US-based engineering and assembly at a 66,000-square-foot Long Island facility expected to be fully operational by Q1 2027.

items.title: China ships 97% of the world's humanoid robots
items.summary: Chinese makers shipped more than 97% of the roughly 19,100 humanoid robots delivered worldwide in the first half of 2026, according to research firm Smart Analytics Global cited by Bloomberg — with Shanghai's Agibot leading at 8,400 units and Hangzhou's Unitree at 5,900. Industrial and commercial applications made up more than 70% of shipments, up from roughly 50% a year earlier, according to the firm.

items.title: DeepSeek buys into Unitree's $9 billion IPO
items.summary: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek is named among the strategic investors in Unitree's IPO filing, joining the robot maker's Shanghai listing at a valuation of about $9 billion. Founder Wang Xingxing said current humanoid and quadruped models have US approvals while future models could face sales restrictions there, according to remarks reported by Global Times.

items.title: Unitree's R1 starts college in Canada
items.summary: St. Clair College in Windsor has taken delivery of a Unitree R1 — what humanoid.guide calls the first of the newly released model to land in North America — purchased from Canadian firm InDro Robotics with backing from the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council. Students will put the four-foot, 29 kg humanoid to work this fall on quality inspection, materials handling and workforce training.

items.title: Avatar Robotics raises $6.5M seed for human-in-the-loop humanoids
items.summary: The San Francisco startup pairs semi-humanoid hardware with remote teleoperators and machine-learning autonomy, shifting tasks from operator control to full autonomy over time, according to the company. The AlleyCorp-led round follows deployments Avatar says have processed more than 900,000 products in live customer facilities, including for a global beauty retailer.

items.title: Nori Robotics aims the compact L3 at labs and living rooms
items.summary: The 145 cm, 40 kg robot pairs a mobile base with two arms and concentrates 16 of its 20 degrees of freedom in the hands, taking on chores from loading a dishwasher to threading a needle, according to the company. Already in production, it is pitched as an affordable entry point into humanoid-style research for education and home-service experimentation.

items.title: UBTECH's $55,000 Cruzr Y1 reports for warehouse duty
items.summary: The 170 cm, 90 kg humanoid blends autonomous mobility with dual-arm manipulation, according to UBTECH, hauling loads up to 10 kg with about four hours of runtime for sorting and material handling around people and equipment. Already in production at roughly $55,000, it is aimed at flexible indoor automation rather than fixed, single-purpose machinery.

items.title: New York bill would keep humanoid robots from teaching
items.summary: Senate Education Chair Shelley Mayer's bill would require school districts and charter schools to adopt written policies barring AI-enabled humanoids from teacher duties — classroom instruction, one-to-one tutoring and grading — after Salamanca paused its Realbotix classroom pilot. Realbotix CEO Andrew Kiguel calls a sweeping statewide prohibition premature, and the legislature takes the measure up when it reconvenes in January.

items.title: Unitree prices its Shanghai IPO at a $9 billion valuation
items.summary: Hangzhou-based Unitree will sell 40.45 million shares at 150.8 yuan apiece — about 10% of the company — raising some 6.1 billion yuan ($900 million) at a 61 billion yuan ($9.04 billion) valuation, with subscriptions opening August 10, according to Reuters. The STAR Market debut would make Unitree mainland China's first listed humanoid robot maker, after 2025 revenue more than quadrupled to 1.7 billion yuan.

items.title: UC San Diego sends humanoid robots into the operating room
items.summary: Teleoperated humanoids completed gallbladder removals in a preclinical animal trial — once alongside a human surgeon and once as a two-robot team, the first surgeries completed by two teleoperated humanoids, according to UC San Diego. Frequent recalibration and control latency made the procedures far slower than dedicated surgical systems, so the work remains proof-of-concept.

items.title: Mitsubishi turns a Kyoto engine line into a humanoid factory
items.summary: Mitsubishi Motors plans to mass-produce Highlanders' roughly 1.75 m humanoid at its Kyoto plant from the first half of 2027, on a repurposed engine production line with capacity for up to 1,000 robots a month, according to the company. The robots will first fill labor gaps in Mitsubishi's own factories, with external sales a later step.

items.title: Billionaire family offices pile into humanoid startups
items.summary: The family offices of Bernard Arnault, Jeff Bezos and Azim Premji are all writing robotics checks — Arnault's venture arm joined London-based Humanoid's Series A, Bezos's firm increased its allocation to Generalist AI, and Premji's office is in talks to lead a round for a general-purpose robot maker, according to Bloomberg. Behind the spree sits a Barclays forecast that the humanoid robot market will grow more than 1,000% within the next decade.

items.title: ROBOTERA aims the wheeled Q5 at hotels, hospitals and museums
items.summary: The service humanoid pairs a stable mobile base with expressive arms and hands precise enough to thread a needle, according to ROBOTERA, plus voice interaction in more than 37 languages backed by DeepSeek models and custom RAG knowledge bases. Already in production, the Q5 is pitched at lobbies, retail and tourism — light service work rather than factory floors.

items.title: Paris startup UMA debuts Northstar, a humanoid that learns by watching
items.summary: The 165 cm, 40 kg prototype from the Rémi Cadène-led firm picks up tasks by watching people and refining the motions through practice, according to UMA, with five-finger hands aimed at gentle, repeatable handling — warehouse sorting and folding clothes rather than athletics. Priced at $70,000, it reads as a signal of where European robotics is heading.

items.title: Why humanoids aren't winning the factory floor yet
items.summary: Economics, not technology, is the barrier, argues Plus One Robotics co-founder Shaun Edwards in The Robot Report: humanoids costing several hundred thousand dollars can't yet beat specialized sorters hitting 1,300–3,000 picks per hour, while the best humanoid demos manage about 1,000 in controlled conditions. The math changes when manufacturing scale drives component costs down — an argument Edwards says favors mass producers like Tesla.

items.title: UBTech books 13,000+ U1 orders ahead of September deliveries
items.summary: Deliveries of the UWORLD U1 home humanoid start September 16, with cumulative orders past 13,361 by the end of June across the Lite, Pro and Ultra models priced from 119,800 to 990,000 yuan, according to UBTech. The company is selling facial expressions, voice interaction and AI conversation — not chores.

items.title: BYD confirms its first humanoid robot lands this month
items.summary: The EV giant will debut its first humanoid this August at its Di Space experience centers, teasing presence and interaction rather than specs, according to a company WeChat post. BYD has run a dedicated embodied-AI unit since late 2024, and executive vice president Stella Li sees robots working as sales demonstrators in BYD stores within one to two years.

items.title: Tau Robotics rents out humanoid house cleaners at $30 an hour
items.summary: The startup has opened a teleoperated humanoid cleaning service for San Francisco homes — remote operators with AI assistance, starting with vacuuming for selected applicants — and CEO Alex Koch concedes today's AI can't yet run the robots autonomously. UC Berkeley's Ken Goldberg is skeptical the machines can do a useful job of cleaning a house.

items.title: Booster Robotics debuts the T2, a humanoid built for research labs
items.summary: The 140 cm, 43 kg biped is pitched as Booster's flagship embodied-AI platform for universities and research teams, with 31 degrees of freedom, Thor T5000 compute and a claimed 7 km/h top speed, according to the company. Already in production, the T2 leans on navigation — stair climbing, 100-meter runs and recovery from falls — rather than fine manipulation.

items.title: Moon Dynamics aims the $60,000 L1 at warehouse lifting
items.summary: Shenzhen-based Moon Dynamics has put the 165 cm, 60 kg L1 into production at $60,000, pitching it at material handling in warehouses, factories and logistics sites. According to the company, the biped carries up to 25 kg on a three-hour charge, tops out at 7 km/h, and uses a millisecond-level control stack to keep its balance when loads shift — with two-finger claws in place of dexterous hands.

items.title: UBTECH points the $25,000 U1 Pro at homes, not factories
items.summary: The 183 cm humanoid, up for pre-order at roughly $25,000, carries 88 degrees of freedom and an emotional language model called Resonance LM, targeting companionship, reception and light tasks like folding clothes, according to UBTECH. Sub-20-millisecond lip sync signals where the priorities lie: presence and interaction over heavy labor.

items.title: Unitree closes in on a $618M Shanghai IPO as the US ban lands
items.summary: The Hangzhou company is finalizing pricing on a STAR Market listing targeting 4.2 billion yuan (about $618 million) after what humanoid.guide calls the fastest sign-off in STAR Market history — a debut that would make Unitree the first humanoid robot developer on China's A-share market. With the FCC's import ban arriving just as Chinese listing preparations peak, Counterpoint Research reckons the timing is 'unlikely to be accidental.'

items.title: China vows to retaliate over the US robot ban
items.summary: China's commerce ministry says it will “resolutely retaliate” and safeguard its interests if Washington insists on the FCC's import ban on new Chinese robots and power inverters, urging the US to withdraw what it calls “erroneous actions” and “unilateral bullying,” according to Reuters. The warning turns last week's ban — which hits humanoid market leader Unitree hardest — into an open trade fight.

items.title: Robot industry splits over the US import ban
items.summary: Security hawks hail the FCC's block on new foreign humanoids as a defining technology-security move, while analysts warn it could slow US physical-AI innovation and may even catch Canadian and European robots, according to experts canvassed by The Robot Report. China has shipped 80–90% of the world's humanoids to date, per IFR figures cited in the piece.

items.title: The US bans new Chinese humanoid robots
items.summary: The FCC is barring imports of new models of Chinese humanoid and quadruped robots, along with grid-connecting power inverters, to shield the US AI buildout from disruption, data theft and cyberattacks, according to a Reuters exclusive. Unitree — holding roughly a fifth of the global humanoid market — is the most exposed name, though already-authorized models can keep shipping for now.

items.title: A $57,590 classroom humanoid sparks a New York backlash
items.summary: Realbotix's M-Series robot “Sally” and its Optio AI assistant are set to join a Salamanca High School classroom this fall — on Seneca Nation territory where about 40% of students are Native American — drawing opposition from teachers' unions and state education officials over privacy, data security and the role of human educators.

items.title: Generative Bionics debuts Gene.01, a smart-skin humanoid
items.summary: The Italian startup's first platform wraps a sensor skin from torso to limbs that detects people before contact and supports guide-by-hand training, according to the company. Built on Italian Institute of Technology research and an $81 million seed led by CDP Venture Capital, Gene.01's first job is welding work with shipbuilder Fincantieri.

items.title: Mitsubishi Motors teams up with Highlanders to mass-produce humanoids
items.summary: Mitsubishi Motors has partnered with University of Tokyo spinout Highlanders to develop and mass-produce AI-equipped humanoid robots, starting with trials on an engine line at its Kyoto plant. The pair are targeting output of 1,000 units a month by the end of 2027, according to the companies.

items.title: A push to ban Chinese humanoids reaches Washington
items.summary: A Daily Signal op-ed urges the FCC to put Chinese humanoid robots on its Covered List — the mechanism used against Huawei gear and DJI drones — casting camera-laden machines like Unitree's $13,500 G1 as mobile data-collection platforms, according to the authors, who cite over $20 billion in Beijing robotics subsidies. The call lands as Rep. John Moolenaar's NDAA amendments seek an assessment of U.S. military infrastructure's dependence on hardware from adversarial foreign suppliers.

items.title: Holiday Robotics breaks cover with FRIDAY, a hands-first wheeled humanoid
items.summary: Seoul-based Holiday Robotics has unveiled FRIDAY, a wheeled humanoid aimed at manufacturing, automotive, semiconductor and logistics work. According to the company, the robot packs 64 degrees of freedom — 40 of them in its hands — along with hot-swappable batteries and a vision-language-skill software stack now in private pilots with industrial partners.

items.title: Kalanick's Atoms raises $1.7B — and it's not betting on humanoids
items.summary: Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick has raised $1.7 billion for Atoms in a round led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Bain Capital and Uber participating, to build AI-driven robots and automation for manufacturing, real estate and transportation. According to Kalanick, humanoids will be good at low-scale tasks in human-designed spaces — high-volume industrial work will go to purpose-built machines.

items.title: Japan's humanoid push moves into factories and airports
items.summary: Japan Airlines is running a two-year Haneda Airport trial of Unitree G1-based humanoids for ground handling with GMO AI & Robotics, Toyota is evaluating prototypes on a components line, and Mitsubishi Motors is targeting 1,000 robots a month as early as 2027, according to humanoid.guide's roundup. METI is backing the push with roughly ¥90 billion a year in robotics support.

items.title: Tesla goes quiet on Optimus volume production
items.summary: Tesla's Q2 shareholder letter drops the previous quarter's language about the Optimus humanoid reaching volume production, according to TechCrunch — in a quarter where capital spending more than doubled and volume-production timelines for the Cybercab, Semi and Megapack 3 all slipped.

items.title: EngineAI opens a humanoid combat league in Shenzhen
items.summary: EngineAI's Ultimate Robot Knockout Legend kicked off in Shenzhen with 32 teams fighting full-size T800 humanoids — a roughly $40,500, 29-joint machine, according to the company — ahead of finals in November–December. The Chinese Institute of Electronics projects China's humanoid robot market will reach about 870 billion yuan by 2030.

items.title: UK's Humanoid raises $152M, calling itself Europe's first humanoid unicorn
items.summary: The London startup behind the wheeled HMND 01 closed a $152 million Series A led by Prime Movers Lab at a $1.35 billion post-money valuation — making it Europe's first pure-play humanoid robotics unicorn, according to the company. Schaeffler and Bosch join as strategic backers, doubling as anchor customer and contract manufacturer ahead of a Q4 2026 beta rollout.

items.title: Hyundai workers strike over Atlas deployment plans
items.summary: Around 35,000 unionized workers at Hyundai's Ulsan complex have begun four-hour walkouts demanding union approval before humanoid robots enter Korean factories — just as Hyundai completes its full takeover of Atlas maker Boston Dynamics. The partial strikes have reportedly already cut output by roughly 5,000 vehicles.

items.title: Verified deployments favor Figure and Agility
items.summary: humanoid.guide's mid-year review finds real industrial humanoid work still concentrated at a handful of named sites: Figure 02 logged 1,250+ hours and 90,000+ parts in its 11-month BMW pilot, while Agility's Digit has passed 65,000 operating hours across nine customer facilities, according to the companies.

items.title: UK's Humanoid puts HMND 01 on wheels for warehouse work
items.summary: The London startup is putting roughly 90% of its engineering into a wheeled version of its HMND 01 robot for shelf stocking and machine feeding — lifting 15 kg and working at about 80% of human speed, according to Humanoid, with CE certification targeted for late 2027.

items.title: AgiBot debuts four robots at WAIC, led by the A3 Ultra humanoid
items.summary: At Shanghai's World AI Conference the company unveiled the 1.74 m, 51-DoF A3 Ultra — running Nvidia's Thor chip with up to eight hours of runtime, according to AgiBot — alongside the X2 EDU education platform, the industrial G2 Max and the 20-DoF OmniHand 3 Ultra-M dexterous hand.

items.title: Weave Robotics puts the home humanoid on sale at $7,999
items.summary: The San Francisco startup has opened orders for Isaac 1, a wheeled home robot that folds laundry, makes beds and tidies rooms autonomously, according to Weave — $7,999 up front or $449 a month, with first deliveries this fall.

items.title: Hyundai moves to take full ownership of Boston Dynamics
items.summary: SoftBank is exercising its put option and Hyundai Motor Group shareholders will buy out its remaining stake in the Atlas maker, according to Hyundai — which says it plans to put Atlas humanoids to work at its Metaplant America factory from 2028.

items.title: LimX Dynamics closes a $200M Pre-IPO round at a RMB 15B valuation
items.summary: The Shenzhen humanoid maker has now raised $400 million in six months — days before showing its Oli robot clearing a room of household chores fully autonomously.

items.title: Toyota spinout Walden Robotics launches with $300M at a $1.1B valuation
items.summary: The Toyota Research Institute spinout led by MIT's Russ Tedrake emerged from stealth with backing from Toyota, Nvidia, Boeing and Samsung — and says its wheeled general-purpose robots have been working at a Toyota plant in North America since February.

items.title: Agility Robotics heads for the stock market at a ~$2.5B valuation
items.summary: The Oregon-based maker of Digit plans to list via a SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI, raising over $620 million — while CEO Peggy Johnson says home humanoids are still a decade out.

items.title: Amazon and Nvidia among backers of Neura Robotics, CNBC reports
items.summary: More Big Tech capital flows into the humanoid race as the German robot maker draws high-profile investors.
